A thorough analysis of the data, as depicted in Figure 12, reveals that there is no strong correlation between build parameters and mechanical properties. In fact, all parameters within the operating window demonstrated satisfactory mechanical performance. This lack of distinction in behavior can be attributed to the uniform microstructures produced during fabrication, which were seemingly unaffected by the parameter set. Alternatively, the small sample size may have been insufficient to capture any cracking that might have occurred, as cracks outside the gauge length would not have influenced the test results. However, it is worth noting that heat-treated specimens did exhibit slightly different behavior, suggesting that post- processing techniques can have a subtle impact on the mechanical properties of the final product. A comparison of the results obtained from different powders, as illustrated in Figure 13, reveals that the PAC powder exhibited higher ultimate tensile strength (UTS), while the Praxair powder demonstrated greater ductility. This disparity can be attributed to the significantly higher carbon content in the PAC powder composition. Furthermore, the orientation of the samples had a profound impact on the curve shape and properties, with the "V" samples consistently displaying lower yield strength, higher UTS, and increased elongation compared to the "H" samples. This orientation-dependent behavior was also observed when comparing as-built versus heat-treated samples, as shown in Figure 14. A concise summary of the yield strength and UTS values is presented in Figure 15, providing a clear visual representation of the differences between the powders and orientations. The results of the as-built and heat-treated specimens are presented in Figure 15, offering a comprehensive overview of the mechanical properties. Despite the relatively low heat treatment applied, the material was able to recover some of its ductility, indicating a positive response to the thermal processing. Notably, the data exhibits a fair degree of scatter, which can be attributed to the fact that all build parameters are represented in the figure. This suggests that the heat treatment effects may be influenced by the specific build conditions, leading to a range of outcomes. Nonetheless, the overall trend indicates that heat treatment can be an effective means of enhancing the ductility of the material, even at relatively low temperatures.
